extracted.intended_audience: general newspaper readers and policymakers (wartime U.S. public)
extracted.subtask_description: Reporting and presentation of military operations, relief efforts, and government actions (including executive orders) during wartime; combines battlefield dispatches, official communiqués, eyewitness quotes and political reaction. Suited to daily newspaper coverage of World War II–era events.

rubrics_metrics.name: A — Develop unified programs and establish policies
rubrics_metrics.description: “(A) To develop unified programs and to establish policies for the maximum use of the nation’s natural and industrial resources for military and civilian needs, for the effective use of the national manpower not in the armed forces, for the maintenance and stabilization of the civilian economy, and for the adjustment of such economy to war needs and conditions;”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Text quoted from the presidential order reproduced in the article. As a reporting/organizational standard, this defines the Director of War Mobilization’s core mandate: unify programs and set policies covering resources, manpower not in the armed forces, and civilian economic stabilization.

rubrics_metrics.name: B — Unify activities of federal agencies
rubrics_metrics.description: “(B) To unify the activities of Federal agencies and departments engaged in or concerned with production, procurement, distribution or transportation of military or civilian supplies, materials and products and to resolve and determine controversies between such agencies or departments, except those to be resolved by the Director of Economic Stabilization under Sec. 3, Title IV of Executive Order 9250; and”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Direct excerpt indicating authority to coordinate and settle disputes among production/procurement/distribution agencies; relevant both as a legal standard and as a reportage point when explaining the new office’s remit.

rubrics_metrics.name: C — Issue directives on policy or operations
rubrics_metrics.description: “(C) To issue such directives on policy or operations to the Federal agencies and departments as may be necessary to carry out the programs developed, the policies established and the decisions made under this order.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies the director’s power to direct other agencies — useful guideline when reporting on the scope and consequences of the Office’s authority or when tracing downstream actions by other agencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duty of agencies to execute directives and report progress
rubrics_metrics.description: “It shall be the duty of all such agencies and departments to execute these directives and to make to the Office of War Mobilization such progress reports as may be required.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A reporting criterion for coverage of governmental coordination: journalists should note obligations placed on agencies and any reporting requirements or evidence of compliance (or noncompliance).

rubrics_metrics.name: Composition and advisory role of the War Mobilization Committee
rubrics_metrics.description: “There is established ... the War Mobilization Committee ... of which the director shall be the chairman ... The committee shall consist, in addition to the director, of the Secretary of War, the Secretary of the Navy, the chairman of the Munitions Assignment Board, the Chairman of the War Production Board, and the Director of Economic Stabilization.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Article reproduces membership and advisory function; reporters should identify committee membership and clarify that the committee serves to advise and consult with the director, as part of explaining governance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Director’s operational flexibility and staffing authority
rubrics_metrics.description: “The Office of War Mobilization may perform the functions, exercise the powers, authority and discretion conferred on it by this order through such officials and such agencies and in such manner as the director, subject to the provisions of this order, may determine. The director shall receive such compensation as the President shall provide and, within the limits of funds which may be made available, may employ necessary personnel and make provision for supplies, facilities and services necessary.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies the director’s discretion in structuring operations and hiring — important to explain how the office will function in practice and its capacity to act without rigid procedural constraints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendment of prior executive orders where conflicting
rubrics_metrics.description: “All prior Executive Orders in so far as they are in conflict herewith are amended accordingly.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Legal consequence to mention when reporting institutional change: note which prior orders or arrangements are displaced or superseded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Office as arbiter of inter-agency disputes (inflation/economic programs)
rubrics_metrics.description: Administrative reporting noted that the Office of War Mobilization 'will be the supreme arbiter of all inter-agency conflicts in the inflation program,' while the Office of Economic Stabilization would handle smaller wage/price issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Though presented as an administrative-source claim rather than a clause of the order, this is a practical standard journalists should report and verify: which office resolves specific disputes (inflation, wages, prices) and where authority truly lies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use official communiqués and broadcasts as primary sources
rubrics_metrics.description: The article repeatedly cites official sources: 'A Middle East air communique issued in Cairo said ...', 'An Italian broadcast reported ...', 'The Cairo announcement ...', 'The Chinese Central News ... reported.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: News reporting standard demonstrated on the page: rely on and attribute official military communiqués, government broadcasts and dispatches for operational details, but clearly label origin and any possible bias.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide precise operational details (locations, units, numbers, losses, tonnage, distances)
rubrics_metrics.description: Examples in the article include: 'thirteen enemy fighters were destroyed ... at the cost of a single American Warhawk', '1,200 tons of condensed and powdered milk, 1,500 tons of flour, 1,000 tons of sugar ...', 'nineteen tons dumped in the Wewak sector ... raised to forty-seven tons ... in two days', and specific place names and distances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Journalistic criterion: include measurable, specific data (units lost, tonnage, miles, place names) to convey scale and allow readers to assess tactical or humanitarian impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attribute claims and note verification status
rubrics_metrics.description: The article marks some claims as unverified or reported only by one side: e.g., 'The broadcast ... other claims ... was not reported immediately,' and headings like 'Damage Is Not Reported.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain skeptical attribution: when publishing enemy or partisan claims, indicate whether independent confirmation exists and avoid presenting unverified claims as fact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include strategic context and analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Passages analyze strategic effects: 'This coordination of effort is enabling Allied fighters and bombers to strike at Axis outposts along the entire central and eastern area of the Mediterranean' and 'thus severely hampered one of the most important of the Axis lines of supply and communication.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reporting should not only describe actions but explain their strategic significance (supply lines, operational coordination, anticipated follow-up operations).

rubrics_metrics.name: Include eyewitness and participant quotes for immediacy
rubrics_metrics.description: The article includes first-person quotes and descriptions from participants: e.g., pilot Curtis M. (Ritchie) Richardson’s observations on naval gunfire and landing operations, and a Canadian airman relaying Montgomery's remarks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use direct quotes from participants to humanize reporting and provide on-the-ground perspective, while indicating the speaker’s role and any possible hearsay chain (e.g., 'in a letter to his parents').

rubrics_metrics.name: Report relief logistics with itemized quantities
rubrics_metrics.description: When covering relief, the article itemizes supplies delivered: 'delivered were 1,200 tons of condensed and powdered milk, 1,500 tons of flour, 1,000 tons of sugar, 500 tons of cotton cloth and smaller quantities of men's, women's and children's clothing.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Humanitarian reporting standard: list kinds and quantities of relief supplies to convey scale and timeliness of aid.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report political reaction and legislative commentary
rubrics_metrics.description: The piece collects responses from senators and officials to Byrnes’s appointment: multiple quoted evaluations from Senators Murray, Taft, Van Nuys, Guffey, Green, Ferguson, etc., and remarks from Price Administrator Brown and Bernard Baruch.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For stories about appointments or institutional change, compile and attribute reactions across the political spectrum, noting endorsements, reservations, and implications for policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publish full text or substantial excerpts of official orders when appropriate
rubrics_metrics.description: The article reproduces the presidential order establishing the Office of War Mobilization and includes its operative sections and Roosevelt’s explanatory statement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When feasible, include verbatim or substantial excerpts of executive orders or legal texts to allow readers to see the precise authority, functions and language being invoked.
